title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its values grouped by depth: a list of lists where the `i`-th inner list holds the values at depth `i`, from left to right.
hints: Which traversal naturally visits nodes one level at a time?
Use a queue. How can you tell where one level ends and the next begins?
Before processing a level, record the queue's current length; pop exactly that many nodes, collecting their values and enqueueing their children.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def levelOrder(self, root: Optional[TreeNode]) -> List[List[int]]:

args.$py: [x for i in range(1,3000) for x in (i,None)]+[3000]

solution.explanation: Run a breadth-first search with a queue. At the start of each round, the queue holds exactly one level, so take its current length, pop that many nodes, record their values as one inner list, and push their children for the next round. Every node is enqueued and dequeued once, so time is O(n); the queue holds at most one level, O(n) space in the worst case.
